tip_diameter.quote: a solidity limit of 1.1, an inlet hub-tip ratio of 0.55, and a tip diameter of 20 inches.

constant_tip_diameter.quote: The configuration chosen had a constant tip diameter of 20 inches, an inlet hub-tip ratio of 0.55, and a hub diameter which increased at the rate required to maintain the selected limiting Mach number for the blade rows.

design_weight_flow.quote: Weight flow, lb/sec (no boundary layer allowance) . . . 57.5

weight_flow_per_unit_frontal_area.quote: Weight flow per unit frontal area, lb/sec . . . 26.4

assumed_stage_polytropic_efficiency.quote: This design procedure with an assumed stage polytropic efficiency of 0.90 established the following design-point characteristics: a pressure ratio of 6.45 and an equivalent weight flow of 57.5 pounds per second at the design equivalent tip speed of 869 feet per second.

design_inlet_conditions.quote: values given are for standard sea-level inlet conditions

design_limits.quote: Aerodynamic limitations used included a relative Mach number limit of 0.7, a solidity of 1.1, and a loading limit (CLσ where CL is the lift coefficient and σ is the blade-element solidity) which increased from 0.8 to 1.0 through the compressor.

velocity_diagram_type.value: symmetrical velocity diagram, constant total enthalpy at all radii, simplified radial equilibrium
velocity_diagram_type.quote: The design was based on a symmetrical velocity diagram with constant total enthalpy at all radii.

boundary_layer_allowance.quote: no attempt was made to provide a boundary-layer allowance.

profile_rotor_stator_exit_vane.value: NACA 65-series blower blade section, 10 percent thick
profile_rotor_stator_exit_vane.quote: The design used the NACA 65-series airfoil scaled down to 10 percent thickness and modified by the addition of 0.0015 times chordal position to the thickness ordinate, designated in reference 7 as the NACA 65-series blower blade section.

constant_camber_and_chord_along_span.quote: In order to simplify construction, the blades were designed with constant camber and chord at all radii of a given blade row rather than using a variable section blade. Thus the solidity varies inversely with the radius in any stage.

meanline_definition.value: NACA 65-series blower mean line (data for CL,i = 1.0 in reference 10, table II) scaled by the design CL,i
meanline_definition.quote: Reference 10 (table II) gives the mean line data for the NACA 65-series blower blade sections with CL,i = 1.0. For the prescribed camber, the coordinates of the mean line and the tangent of the angle of the mean line were obtained by multiplying by the design value of CL,i.

turning_rule.value: Δβ = mα + b; m(β, σ), b(β, CL,i, σ) from charts (fig. 5)
turning_rule.quote: Charts (fig. 5) were prepared for the determination of m (as a function of β and σ) and b (as a function of β, CL,i, and σ) from the available data on 65-series blower blade sections.

CL_definition.quote: It was also possible to establish the actual value of CL from the relation CL = 2UtY/(Wmσ)

angle_convention.value: β (absolute inlet-air angle) and β' (inlet-air angle relative to rotor) measured with respect to axis; α angle of attack; Δβ turning angle
angle_convention.quote: β absolute inlet-air angle, measured with respect to axis (deg) (fig. 3); β' inlet-air angle relative to rotor, measured with respect to axis (deg) (fig. 3)

station_numbering_E52B18.value: 0 ahead of IGV; 1,3,...,19 ahead of rotors 1..10; 2,4,...,20 ahead of stators 1..10; 21 ahead of exit vanes; 22 after exit vanes
station_numbering_E52B18.quote: 0 station ahead of inlet-guide vanes; 1,3,5 . . . 19 station ahead of rotors of 1st, 2nd . . . 10th stages; 2,4,6 . . . 20 station ahead of stators of 1st, 2nd . . . 10th stages; 21 station ahead of exit vanes; 22 station after exit vanes

igv_count_and_type.quote: The inlet stage comprised 36 circular-arc constant-thickness sheet-metal guide vanes, 25 rotor blades, and 27 stator blades.

igv_material_thickness.quote: Figure 2. - Inlet guide vane. Number 14-gage (0.083) mild steel.

igv_sketch_dimensions.quote: Figure 2 dimension labels as printed: '3.75" rad.', '0.03" rad.', trailing-edge detail '0.25"' and '0.020', planform '1.78"' and '10.00" rad.'

igv_original_design_rule.value: design rule for convergent annuli (reference 7 of RM E53H10), with compressibility and hub-taper corrections applied
igv_original_design_rule.quote: The guide vanes for the compressor were originally designed with the design rule for convergent annuli presented in reference 7.

igv_incidence_original_and_reset.quote: Resetting the guide vanes to a -5° incidence angle in accordance with airfoil cascade data resulted in good agreement of the absolute flow angles with the design values (fig. 4).

igv_setting_method.value: set with a straight edge between LE and TE; about 0.5 to 1 deg deviation from a chord-line setting
igv_setting_method.quote: The manner in which the guide vanes were set with a straight edge between the leading and trailing edges of the vanes causes a deviation of approximately 0.5° to 1° from a chord-line setting.

igv_design_in_E52B18.value: sheet-metal IGVs, sections chosen by the methods of references 11 and 12 of RM E52B18
igv_design_in_E52B18.quote: Sheet-metal inlet guide vanes were selected to provide the turning as established by the inlet-stage velocity diagram.

measured_design_speed_peak_pressure_rati.quote: At design speed the peak compressor pressure ratio was 7.52, the maximum weight flow was 56.2 pounds per second, and the peak adiabatic efficiency was 0.83.
